methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 4 same-sector + similar-valuation-tier peers in Drones & Autonomous. Range: $800M - $7.6B.

private.name: Joby Aviation
private.rationale: Same sector (Drones & Autonomous), same stage (Public), post-money $6.86B

data.narrative:
Archer Aviation, a publicly listed autonomous aircraft developer in the Drones & Autonomous sector, carries a current market valuation of $3.33 billion following over $1.5 billion in total capital raised. The valuation analysis draws from a peer set of four same-sector competitors spanning similar valuation tiers: Zipline ($7.6B, Series G), Joby Aviation ($6.9B, public), Nuro ($6.0B, Series G), and Elroy Air ($800M, Series B).

Peer-median triangulation yields an implied valuation of $6.4 billion, with the four-company peer set spanning a range of $800 million to $7.6 billion. This method is directly applicable given the homogeneity of the comparable universe in stage maturity and sector focus. The median peer valuation sits $3.1 billion above Archer's current public market price, suggesting either market undervaluation relative to the peer set or execution risk priced into public equity that private financing rounds may not fully reflect.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $5.5 billion to $7.4 billion centered on the peer median of $6.4 billion. Key uncertainties include the dispersion within the peer set—a 9.5x spread from low to high—and limited public market comparables (zero public peers identified), which constrains confidence in market-implied multiples. The wide peer range reflects heterogeneous technology maturity and commercialization timelines across autonomous systems, limiting the precision of median-based approaches.
